marks.why: 'This is' points at nothing: picture is a trader, not the coin, so a sound-off viewer has no subject. 5.3s is a long, museum-label hook; 'one of the earliest known coins of pure gold' reads as a placard.
marks.fix_line: Nobody trusted money. / This coin? One of the earliest known in pure gold.
marks.fix_picture: Frame 1: extreme close-up of the gold coin glinting, then hard cut to trader squinting and scale tipping on 'nobody trusted money'. Coin must be on screen when 'This coin' caption lands.

marks.why: Two unfamiliar proper/jargon words back to back (Lydia, electrum) at the exact moment the hook needs to pay off. Textbook tone; strangers swipe here.
marks.fix_line: Lydia's older coins were electrum: gold and silver, mixed by nature.
marks.fix_picture: Keep the lump splitting into two colours but caption 'GOLD + SILVER' over the split, not 'ELECTRUM'.

marks.why: Fine beat but restates the previous picture's idea (mixed colours) with another static row of coins.
marks.fix_picture: Fast push along the row of coins, each shade flashing as it passes, so the frame is moving.

marks.why: 4.6s for a problem the viewer already gets; 'test stone' slows it. Second scale shot repeats the 0s picture.
marks.fix_line: Weigh it? Test-stone it? Still guessing.
marks.fix_picture: Skip the scale (already used); single shot of coin streaked on black stone, streak colour shifting.

marks.why: Payoff crammed into one 6.4s run-on line with a 'baked it in salt until...' clause; captions at 2-3 words lose the cause/effect.
marks.fix_line: So Sardis refiners packed it in salt and baked it. / Until the silver was gone. The gold, basically pure.
marks.fix_picture: Cut on the sentence break: glowing salt-packed pots, then pot cracked open revealing bright gold grain.

marks.why: Good pattern break; eyebrow reaction works.
Who stamps and why is implied only; 'pure gold, pure silver' crammed with commas; silver arrives unannounced.
marks.fix_line: Stamp a lion and a bull. On pure gold. On pure silver.
marks.fix_picture: Two separate die strikes timed to each 'On pure...' caption: gold strike, then silver strike.

marks.why: Short, name is cushioned by the crowned silhouette; hedge intact.
Weak, museum-label ending: weight and findspot after the climax. Only redeemed because the real photo is the first true reveal.
marks.fix_line: This one: about 8 grams, from Sardis.
marks.fix_picture: Real Met photo of stater 26.59.2 slams in full-frame with a slow zoom on the lion and bull, so it reads as the reveal.

marks.why: 'All because...' into 'Nobody trusted money' is a clean loop; coin back into trader's hand matches frame 1 if frame 1 includes the trader.
marks.fix_picture: End on the coin in the trader's palm, matching the new opening close-up.

rewrite:
Nobody trusted money.
This coin? One of the earliest known in pure gold.
Lydia's older coins were electrum: gold and silver, mixed by nature.
But the mix varied.
Weigh it? Test-stone it? Still guessing.
So Sardis refiners packed it in salt and baked it.
Until the silver was gone. The gold, basically pure.
Great. Now prove it.
Stamp a lion and a bull. On pure gold. On pure silver.
Croesus gets the credit.
This one: about 8 grams, from Sardis.
All because...
